newsitem.title: USA: Texas tornado death toll at 28, search winds down.
newsitem.headline: Texas tornado death toll at 28, search winds down.

text.p: Rescuers on Thursday will call off the search for more victims of the devastating tornado believed to have killed 28 people in Jarrell, Texas, a police spokeswoman said.

Searchers combing the rubble of a rural neighbourhood in this central Texas town said 27 bodies had been found along with remains believed to be those of a 28th victim of a tornado that swept through the area on Tuesday.
"We believe 28 people are dead," Texas Department of Public Safety spokeswoman Laureen Chernow said. "There are additional remains they believe will turn out to be that of the 28th person."
Residents of the Double Creek Estates subdivision who survived the tornado will be allowed to return to their neighbourhood after police end the search for more victims at noon, she said.
"(Rescuers) want to make one last swing (through the area) to make sure everything has been taken care of," Chernow said.
Four victims have been positively identified two days after the tornado cut a swath through Jarrell with winds of more than 200 miles (320 km) per hour, she said.
